utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, welcome. Before we start with the next witness, let me mention two matters. The first is the Chamber decided not to sit tomorrow, to cancel the hearing of tomorrow, but we will sit on Monday morning. Thank you for your co-operation, Mr. Tolimir. The second issue has something to do with exhibits again, and because I think everybody would appreciate to have some guidance, I would like to read out our procedural way to deal with it. As the Chamber mentioned during the session on the 18th of March this year, the Prosecution has submitted a number of exhibits associated with witnesses' prior testimony as a part of its motion pursuant to Rule 92 ter. Some of these exhibits were admitted through the witness in prior proceedings. Others were simply used with the witness during the prior testimony. Of this latter category, some were admitted through other witnesses in the prior proceedings, while others were not admitted at all. In both, the Rule 92 ter decision of 3rd of November, 2009, and during the session on 18th of March, 2010, the Chamber has repeatedly drawn a distinction between these different categories of exhibits. Accordingly, the Chamber requests that the Prosecution to communicate a list of exhibits proposed for admission in association with the prior testimony, clearly indicating to which category each exhibit belongs. Following the procedure, this procedure enables the Chamber to be in a position to admit the exhibits associated with the prior written statement or transcript once the conditions of Rule 92 ter paragraph A are met, that is the witness first is present in court; secondly, is available for cross-examination and questioning by the Judges; and thirdly, the tests that the written statement or transcript accurately reflects his or her declaration and what he or she would say if examined. The Chamber considers that those exhibits following within the first category, that is those which were admitted through the witness in prior proceedings are necessarily associated with the prior testimony forming integral part thereof and will be admitted accordingly. The Chamber otherwise, leaves it to the parties to explicitly seek the admission of any other exhibits connected to such prior testimony, such as those which were used with but not admitted through the witness at the time the witness appears for cross-examination, should they consider it necessary. However, the Chamber stresses that before seeking admission of any exhibit not admitted through the witness during his prior testimony, the parties should consider their relevance to the instant case, and whether they are and inseparable and indispensable part of the prior testimony, without which the prior testimony will lose probative value or will become incomprehensible. The Chamber will deal with any submissions in relation to this issue as they arise. This Chamber further notes that since the start of this case, there have been some exhibits which were submitted in connection with some witnesses' prior testimony in the Prosecution's 92 ter motion, but which the Prosecution did not tender when the witness appeared in court in this case. The Chamber wishes to clarify that it does not consider that these exhibits have been properly tendered merely by way of the inclusion in the 92 ter motion. Should the parties consider it necessary, each remains free to move for the admission of any exhibit which has not already been admitted in this case and which, in the view of the moving party, is inseparable and indispensable from the prior testimony of Rule 92 ter witnesses who have already appeared in this case. In the future, however, each party should raise any concerns regarding the inclusion of exhibits related to prior testimony at the time the witness appears in court. This procedure will apply equally to any exhibits accompanying Rule 92 ter testimony proffered by the Defence during the presentation of its case. I hope that clarifies the situation for all future witnesses and exhibits. Thank you. Now, it's up to you, Mr. McCloskey, to call the next witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We are continuing with investigator Janc and should finish up the map book evidence relatively soon. utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understand.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey is continuing his examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Certainly not a MFI form as it is recorded in the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, we've got to distinguish between MIF and MFI or we are in big trouble. But I know that is well known to the Court Reporter, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, this, Mr. Janc, is the MIF form for what you had referenced for this map in the index of your book. Can you tell us just briefly what is a MIF form, for the Court?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, again, MIF form, anyone create when submit the evidence into the evidence unit, so whenever I get, for example, as an investigator knew evidence, I create such form which basic data in it. And then I, together with this form, submit this evidence into evidence unit when it gets stamped and later on archived.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Can you tell by looking at this form where this original map to your left reflected in it, where it came from, where the OTP got it from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we have the evidence description, what it says this map is part of the Drina Corps collection. As I was testifying about the other day, so -- and this map was seised on 13 of December, 2004, and then we have difference information by whom it was seised and from whom and is such information. So evidence description would usually give you a synopsis of what this evidence is and when and where it was seised and from whom.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. So just in looking at this map to your left shoulder, is that, as far as you know, from your knowledge and experience, an original map from the Drina Corps collection?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm quite sure because I've seen a lot of those. I think, if not all of them, at least two times I have reviewed all of them in our archive, so I have unfolded those maps several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we can see that this map is not in what would be a commercial shape, it's in sort of a funny shape, there's no legend at the bottom of it, there's nothing on the top. Can you explain how a map like this would be -- would have been created, if you know?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think these maps were created by the VRS, and these are the working maps and we can see they were stick together from many pieces. Usually at the back you can see the stickers. Also so they were stick together in order to get the area of their interest, so and then they have made these markings on them according to their needs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. If we could go back to e-court page 6 of the map book. 6196.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I don't know if anyone recalls, but originally this particular exhibit, I think I had some question because it shows that Kladanj is part of the Drina Corps; yet, at the same time, the black line that goes north and south, roughly, is clearly marked as the confrontation line, and that is the Muslim or BiH side of the confrontation line. So I offer you, could you take a look briefly at that map which you have told us was the basis of this drawing and see if that reflection of Kladanj being in the Drina Corps is actually noted on that map as part of the outline. I think you can stand up briefly and just take a look.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perhaps audio-visual can zero in on the map with the other part of the screen and so the Court can get a better idea of what this map looks like, as it's just the practicality. They are going to have to zero in. We should know where Kladanj is by this stage.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: But can you focus. That's great. And a little more to give the Court a bit of an idea, and let's try to stay in Bosnia, if we can. Sorry, audio-visual for catching you like this off guard.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could you point to Kladanj on the map so audio-visual can find your finger and blow it up even more.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's here. This is Kladanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Audio, can you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you move, perhaps, the camera should go -- another camera -- yes, that would be, yes, that is helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Perfect. Keep going camera, please. If that's all you can do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Could you outline with your finger the border that's outlined on the map that shows the border of the Drina Corps?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the line and down south.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And can you tell, was that line written in by somebody or was it part of the commercial printing process, do you know what I mean?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was done by the VRS, so it's not part of the commercial process.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. All right. Well --

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And please, Your Honours, if you have any questions, I welcome them, we are just trying to go as we can here to explain that. So now let's -- staying with the map book, could we go now to e-court page 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I recall you have testified previously about one of the maps that this was based upon, and we have gone to the evidence room, and this map to your right is from the ERN that you referenced. utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was seised during the Bratunac -- not Bratunac, but Zvornik Brigade search in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I will try to because we are always using it as MIF, but I think it stands for mini indexing form, something like that, but I'm not 100 per cent sure, but I think that's what it stands for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. If you can take a look at this, the MIF for this map, and does that tell you where this came from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah. That's what I was testifying about. So it was seised on 6th of March, 1998, during the Zvornik Brigade search.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Can you tell us, just in your own -- as your memory -- this, was it the Zvornik Brigade, what, in your view, was this, this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is -- I think this one is -- let me. Yeah, it is. Krivaja 1995. I was looking for written text on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: First of all, what is Krivaja 1995, can you remind us of that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And could you, again, approach this map and point to the area of Baljkovica so that we can -- and audio-visual can do the same thing and to the area Baljkovica where the Muslim column broke through to the Muslim lines. utterances.text: So these are the ones.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what are those arrows, in your mind, designed to depict?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is the -- these arrows depict the movement of the Muslim column out of Srebrenica up to the north.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay. Now, let's go back to e-court page 7, to your map book. 6196. Could we blow that up one more time with those three arrow-heads being in the centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now, we see on this map that we started with, that you have said is based in part on Krivaja 1995 map, these arrows that are in red that start off at Jaglici and Susnjari, what are they based upon? utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Now I would like to go to same -- the map book page 11.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Your Honours, we have the original here, and we have a very fine reproduction for you, but I can display it, if you'd like so we can see that. It's ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if we could just get a little help, we can just put that under the clip so the -- so we can see it. That's great, thank you. That's 65 ter 934.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And that's an original, is it not, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, it is the original.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right. And if we can do the same thing with the map that is on e-court page 12, map book page 10. Thank you, audio-visual for zeroing in on that. utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, do you recall where 933 came from, what collection?

utterances.text: It's the same collection, it's Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so the previous map, 934, what collection was that from?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Also Drina Corps collection.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: There should be an English translation associated with this, just a -- at 65 ter 933. Once we get good at this, all the rest of it will be downhill. You are looking for just an A-4 size sheet with English on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, could you please repeat the number of the map you are looking for. There's some problems to find the right one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Should be under associated documents with 65 ter 00933. Ms. Stewart has got it up and we are getting closer. Okay. Thank you. That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And I'm just -- is there any date -- date on these maps, on this map right here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean this one? Yes, there is a date, 27 of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And what is the date above that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is 12th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: So can you just tell us what do you think this is, just briefly. I don't want a big analysis, but, just, what do you think this map was that was found in the Drina Corps? I mean, we see the dates, 12 July, is it correct that the handwritten part next to that says, "Srebrenica was Serbian and it is Serbian," and then at 27 July it says, "And Zepa is Serbian." What does that tell you about this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That was map was created, obviously, after the attacks on Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves and after their fall. So by the VRS again because we see the handwritten text on the top and the bottom by General Radislav Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, excuse me, we don't have the same map on the screen as we see there and you commented there. It's a different one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I apologise. I didn't notice that. We need to go to 933 -- sorry, 934. That is my fault. This is 934.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Is it part of the map book we received as hard copy?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes. If you see e-court page 12 and e-court page 14, we've used pieces of that -- of that map but not the whole map, so this is the whole map with the writings to give you context where it came from. But we are not --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Isn't it page 10 of the map book?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: No, no. Actually, page 10 of the map book, yes, correct. Page -- e-court page 12, but we still don't have the right map up on the screen. We thought this one currently was 933. Can you read the yellow sticky up in the corner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it says 933, so the ERN of this map should be 0438 -8412.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We may have got it wrong in e-court. Give us a minute, we'll sort it out. Perhaps audio-visual could get it up on the screen, zero in on it a bit. I'm sure it's in there. We probably misnumbered it. So we'll keep looking, thank you. It should be just a second.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What we have on the screen now seems to be page number 9 in the map book, but, if I understood you correctly, we need the next page, number 10 of the map book.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's correct, that's what we have misnumbered, Mr. President, because we've already gone over the one that's on the screen now, but I think we are close to tracking it down, and I really don't have anything else to say about it. It's the map on the board, if audio-visual could zero in on it, I would, of course, like to find it in e-court so that we know it's there for anyone that wants access to it. That's why we print out these in actual size so that you can use them. They are convenient in the computer to zero in on because they do actually blow up, if you want to look on the computer in specific places.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This seems now to be part of the map we see in the original behind the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Well, we are getting closer. That's the one we've already seen. That's page 10 -- or, yes, that's page 10 of the map book, but the original that goes with it, the purpose of this testimony this afternoon, it seems to be lost in e-court. We'll be able to get that in e-court, Mr. President, it will take a few minutes. Otherwise, if the map is here -- and I don't have any further questions except that I can just wrap up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, is this a good reflection, does this reflect the kind of work you were doing in making this map book and going to these maps and is this the kind of information this map book was based upon?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. In this map number 10, which we can see on the screen now, was created part out of this map which we can see on the wall, and the other part are different two maps which were scanned and then everything was electronically much together, and then we just cut out the part of the map we have been interested in. So that's part of that map, the right part of the map we see on the screen is, indeed, part of this original map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: At this time then, Your Honours, I would offer the map book into evidence, and that is 06196 and also the electronic copies of the Krivaja 1995 map, which was 00907. The electronic copy of the one we see there now with the handwriting on the side, which is the one we've lost, 00933, currently, but we are going to have to get it a better number than that. Sorry, it will be the same number, it will just be identified. And map 934, which was the map with the deployment of the forces that we had seen on page 10, and map 06214 was the map that -- or the boundaries of the Drina Corps that included Kladanj, the Muslim town of Kladanj in their border. And I think at this stage, I will leave it at that. I don't think we need to see the MIF or any of that material. That was just for information. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, did I understand you correctly that you are tendering them as five separate exhibits?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, those separate maps, yes. The map book and all its contents, one exhibit.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: They all will be received, and I think, because of some confusion, is it perhaps appropriate to have the break now, and during the break you could liaise with the Registry to have the right numbers. And we can, after the break, receive the right exhibit numbers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm told it's fixed, so 933 should come up as 933.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'm told we can have the exhibit numbers now, all five documents will be received as separate exhibits.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Those will be Exhibit P104 through P108, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And if -- I did see that it was fixed, we do have it on the screen, if we could just, perhaps, get the witness to confirm that this is the one we've been talking about that's over his left shoulder?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, that's the same map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And so it is 933, we are back on track.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, everyone for your patience.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Excuse me. For me, it's not clear yet. You tendered five different documents, that means one map book and four documents. We have heard now that we have one number, P104, for all five exhibits together. Sorry, I didn't realise that. P104 through P108. Everything is fine now. We will have our first break now and resume at 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, did you finish your examination-in-chief, it was not absolutely clear for me?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, I did, Mr. President. And we do have reproductions of those four maps, if the Court would like them at some point. Ms. Stewart has them here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, do you have cross-examination for this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I do have some 20 questions or so for this witness. Thank you, if you allow me.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please go ahead.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And once again, I would like to greet all those present and also the witness, and I have a few questions for you, witness. Mr. Janc, you were mentioned here as an investigator of the Prosecution, that was on page 11224 of the transcript, and you were appointed as a member of the investigating team for Srebrenica and the Tolimir case. My question for you: Could you please describe the structure of your team and what is the role of that -- what is your role in that team?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. In our team, there are three investigators, and I would say five lawyers, and then Case Manager and some language staff, so that's part of the Tolimir trial team. So my role as an investigator is a usual investigative role, so we are conducting interviews with witnesses, victim, suspects, then we have a lot of analysing job. I'm preparing the reports. Then we are collecting evidence, submitting them to evidence unit so, and, this kind of stuff. So any investigative-related tasks.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Please tell us what do you mean when you say the evidence unit. What is that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: When I say the evidence unit, it means there is a unit within the OTP which is in charge of dealing with all the evidence which came into the ICTY and later presented in the courtroom. So they are in charge of all the evidence, so when I got, for example, the evidence on the field, I submit, together with the MIF form, this evidence into the unit, and they are in charge of stamping it then and then putting this -- if it is in written form on a system in electronic format, and then store it in vault, so that's their role.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell me, please, how many translators do you have because you said there are three investigators, five lawyers, and a number of language staff. So how many translators do you have? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Directly on our team in Tolimir trial team, there is -- there are two permanent, and then is a language pool which is in charge of the numerous translations for the other teams also, so I think there are two permanent translators -- language assistants to our team.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell the Trial Chamber, please, do you work independently, or do you work according to somebody's instructions? In other words, whom do you get your instructions from, and whom do you get assignments from? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we also get the assignments mainly from the senior trial attorney and the other trial attorneys and the lawyers. So these are the main people which we get these instructions from, but we also do some job on our own initiatives and then we inform about our findings about our new discoveries, the lawyers and the STA. And I apologise, I didn't mention before in our team is also an analyst.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. Please tell me, is Mr. McCloskey the -- at the head of your team? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, he is senior trial attorney, and he is the head. You can say something like that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. As a member of the Prosecution team in the Tolimir case, are you obliged to abide by a duty to keep professional secrets secret?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, we are obliged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you, for instance, speak in public independently about issues that are relevant to the Prosecution case in this trial, in the Tolimir case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot speak publicly without a certain permissions which should be given to me.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it your duty, as a member of the investigating team of the Prosecution, to protect the interests of the Prosecution and to co-ordinate your actions and your positions with those of the Prosecution? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you be allowed to speak in public and to actually speak and take positions that differ from those from the official position of the Prosecution of the Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not easy comment on that because it's a combined question. Yes, I would be allowed to speak in public, if I have certain permission, so and in that permission is also a kind of instruction about what I'm entitled to talk about, to speak about, and, basically, it wouldn't be possible to talk about something which differ from the official position of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, Mr. Janc, I apologise for erroneously addressing you as Mr. Binc [phoen] since this is not going to be the last time that you appear as a witness in this case, could you tell me, please, do you, in any way, have any impact on the actual formation of the position of the Prosecution? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Object to vagueness. As the previous question, official position or position, I don't -- how does the witness know what that means. I think he is trying his hardest, but I have no idea -- if he could explain what he means by that, he can --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, could you explain it a little bit further. What are you asking?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question number 7 for Mr. Janc was the following: Would he be allowed to speak in public by diverging from the official positions of the Prosecutor, and he said yes, with permission and with instructions as to what he could -- what issues he could address. And that is why now in my next question I want to know if he is allowed to speak in public independently, and as this is not going to be his last time that he is appearing as a witness, my question now is: Would he actually, in any way, have an impact on the way the Prosecution articulates it's position in the Tolimir case? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is, again, the same question and we heard the objection of Mr. McCloskey to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same objection. The Prosecution is not a political party. The Prosecutor makes some positions diplomatically in this institution. It may be a fine question, but what does he mean.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am not sure, Mr. Tolimir, if this is the right person, the witness, Mr. Janc, to explain how the Prosecution, as an institution, articulates its position. He is an investigator employed by the Prosecution of this Tribunal. He can't speak for the Prosecution of the Tribunal. You should clarify, please, your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. My clarification is as follows: I see that the problem here is the word that I used, "official position," but the Prosecutor actually has an official position in this case, and my question is: Whether Mr. Janc can, in any way, propose any -- anything to the Prosecutor in shaping their position, for instance, Mr. McCloskey's, or does he actually abide by the official position as presented here in this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Same objection. This is requiring Mr. Janc to guess what he is talking about, position. Position on what? Position on Serbia entering into the EU? Position on whether or not we should go on to a site visit? Position on evidence? What position?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think it could help if I rephrase your question, Mr. Tolimir. Do you, Mr. Janc, have any influence on the way the Prosecution in this case is dealing with this case? Have you a certain influence on Mr. McCloskey and his team how to deal with this case?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Your Honour, no, no, I don't have any such influence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Presiding Judge. Perhaps the following questions will make this clearer to the witness. In any case, for the most part, I have received my answer, since the answer was actually yes. Thank you. Perhaps the next clarifying question may be this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, the answer was no, not yes.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. I'm content with the answer. I can't follow it on the transcript though because it's not in Serbian.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My next question of the witness, as an OTP investigator, is he obliged to also seek out any exculpatory evidence?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, all the time.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you identified any such exculpatory evidence in the Tolimir case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I did several of them, and in case I came across such evidence, I immediately forward the information to Janet Stewart, who disclosed this information to you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you recall a particular document and what it referred to?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, from the top of my head, I would not be able to recall such document right now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Janc, can you tell us what jobs do you have with the Prosecution of this Tribunal in addition to the tasks you are regularly assigned as part of a team in this case? We have also heard something about your educational background. In any case, could you please tell us anything more about your other duties?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is no other duties. There are just these investigative duties, tasks which I have been talking about before, and that's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this apply to the other members of the team working on this case as well?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I would say so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. When you testified last, you said you were a Slovenian citizen. Were you, at some point in time, also an SFRY citizen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed. When I was born, I was born as an SFRY citizen.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. At page 26, lines 19 to 23, you explained that the map collection was put together by the trial team, and you explained that the geographical information system assisted in that process in the selection and processing of maps. My question of you is this: Did you personally participate in the creation of any point maps, when used as part of the atlas that was presented on the 15th of April, 2010, for the first time in this case?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So I haven't personally created that map, but I was present at some points where some of those maps were created, but not for all of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, tell us this, please: A moment ago during examination-in-chief, you said that the map behind you was seised during a search carried out by the Tribunal alongside NATO; is that correct or have I misunderstood you?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I testified about. Yes, the map on my right-hand side, the Krivaja 1995 map, that's one which was seised at that time in 1998.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. A moment ago you said that a map was seised from the Zvornik Brigade. This makes it two. During the NATO operation, were any other maps seised and, if so, could you tell us how many?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know a lot of other stuff, documents were seised at that time. Yes, and I am sure there were also other maps because I have such -- such a table, I think, on my desk of the -- all the Zvornik Brigade seised maps. So there is a number of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is it customary for an army which fought the VRS to take part in the process of collecting evidence for these Tribunals? I have in mind NATO because they did so, and that was also confirmed by a number of witnesses in this case.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think it was nothing wrong with it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I wasn't asking you whether there was anything wrong with it, but whether it was customary for an armed force, which was the opposing side to the VRS, to collect evidence used to be in a case such as this one heard before this Tribunal?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: This is well beyond the scope, into an area of politics and geopolitics, and I would object.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If the witness can give the account of his knowledge, then it could be appropriate, but Mr. Tolimir, you should be focused on what this witness could give evidence about.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Presiding Judge. I believe this is an important issue because it concerns the collection of evidence, because a party to the conflict collects evidence against the opposing party. I merely wanted to put this to the witness and get an answer which would be either a yes or a no, and I think the witness can answer that. I did not intend to go into the sphere of politics.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm afraid I cannot comment on that because it was a long time ago in 1998, and so I cannot comment on that, so I was not part of this institution at this time, so I don't want to go into this decision, discussions about the decisions, so I cannot comment to that, I am afraid.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please have map number 9. It is the map book 65 ter number 06196, indicating the deployment of VRS forces as well as those of the 2nd Corps of the Army of B&H.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think you are referring to page 9 of the map book, e-court page 11.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. I wanted to see the map number 9, if that could be shown. Thank you. This is what I wanted. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: We can see here that the positions of the VRS and of the 2nd Corps of the AB&H are approximately similar to those indicated on maps 5 and 6. My question is this: When producing the map, did you take into account the situation as it was on the ground, and did you take the borders of the enclave to be as those outlining the territory controlled by the AB&H or did you take the borders as agreed between the VRS, the Army of B&H and UNPROFOR when the agreement on the demilitarised zone was concluded? That would be my question.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: We mostly relied on data which we found on the maps created by the VRS, as you can see it here. So we have used, for example, the borders, the red and the blue lines within the enclave to create our maps. So we have used these sources which I explained in detail -- in detail during my examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown map number 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Should be e-court 8.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness also be shown the Prosecutor 65 ter number 3. Thank you. I see one document here. But these are actually two agreements signed by Ratko Mladic and Sefer Halilovic on the 8th of May, 1993. I'm interested in Article 1 of the agreement on the demilitarisation of Srebrenica and Zepa, concluded between Lieutenant-General Ratko Mladic and General Sefer Halilovic on May 8, 1993, in the presence of General Philippe Morillon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, is there an English translation? I'm told there's no English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is 65 ter page 3 in English and 2 in the B/C/S. It is shown here. You can see what the number is on the top of the page. I will read out for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: This is my question: Article 1 of this agreement, at page 3 in the English and 2 in the B/C/S, which is relevant to the production of documents, of maps of Srebrenica and Zepa is --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There's no English translation. You are referring to page 2 -- page 3 of the English translation. We don't have any.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is Prosecutor 65 ter page 1 in English. 65 ter number 3. Prosecution document. 65 ter number 3, Prosecution document page 1 in the English version.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I am, again, told there is no English translation under this number.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Defence received this document in both English and B/C/S, and the number was 65 ter 3. Perhaps Prosecution could assist us?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I think the Prosecution is in deep deliberations. Can you assist us, Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We haven't heard of this document as used before, so we haven't been able to double-check if it's got an English translation. It does and we can eventually dig it up, and I'm not sure how long it will take us, but we can find that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But, Mr. Tolimir, not to lose time, you could read out the specific portion and then we will have it -- the translation on the record, and the witness can listen to it. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused, however, please read slowly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. It is Article 1 of the agreement. I quote. Thank you: "To demilitarise the areas of Srebrenica and Zepa. The demilitarised areas will include the area inside the confrontation lines. UNPROFOR commander shall, following consultations, mark exact boundaries on the ground. At a later stage, the parties to this agreement can agree orally or in writing to enlarge the area of the demilitarised zone." That is Article 1 of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My question is this, you can see the text, and I'm certain that both the Chamber and the Prosecutor are familiar with this document, and I believe it will eventually be found in English. My question of the witness is this: When determining the boundaries of the enclave, did you have in mind the agreement on the demilitarisation and the lines of confrontation between the VRS and Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina as they were in May 1993? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: My answer would be that we relied upon the maps which were created by the VRS mainly, and the area of the enclaves which was at the time, which means in July 1995. So this document is from 1993, so I think that we -- we have not considered this document, but we relied on the maps which were the closest to the events of the fall of Srebrenica and Zepa enclaves.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I seek to tender this document and I will have the next question of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I won't object, but if the General could make an effort to have English, we'd appreciate it. Also, if he could follow the rule in providing us materials he is going to use for cross-examination. This would have avoided this particular problem.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This document will be marked for identification, depending on receiving and up loading an English translation.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This will be Exhibit D21 marked for identification, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. On your request, I read out Article 1 of the agreement. And we sent Article 1 of the agreement to the Prosecution by e-mail, and I believe they already have it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: My exterior question is this: Was it important to have information on the situation with the demilitarised zone, as it was in May 1993 when the overall process with the maps was underway?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I think not. The important information was what it was on the ground in 1995, in July of 1995. That was the most important in creation of these maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is this piece of information important to analyse the cause of the conflict between the two parties and a possible solution they have agreed upon?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Important for what? You mean for creation of these maps?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it important, for example, for this Chamber which needs to decide about the conflict and its causes between the two sides who were parties to this agreement, was it important to have the boundaries of the demilitarised zone known as they were at the time when it was actually declared a demilitarised zone?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid I cannot answer this question, if it would be important. You know, it's kind of -- everything might be important, but so -- but for creation of other maps, we didn't seek these documents to be of such important that we would use it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc. For the transcript, I'd like to state that in 1993, the Srebrenica demilitarised zone encompassed an area of 5 and a half square kilometres, as we will see a bit later on a map. It was 5.5 times 2.5 square kilometres. We will look at map number 5 and you will see the difference in size. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: What is your question, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My question is this, could we please have map number 5 first, and then the witness can tell us whether the demilitarised zone was enlarged in relation to the agreement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Number 5 should be in e-court, page number 7.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We can see the map now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would kindly ask the witness to indicate the boundaries of the zone, he needn't necessarily agree with the size I mentioned, and it is up to you to decide upon, but I would just like him to indicate the zone itself.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it is on the bottom part of this map, if you scroll down. So you can see the line which goes around Srebrenica and with the letters from A up to M. These dots and the letters are the DutchBat check-points, and this is the situation as it was on the ground in July 1995.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Let's stay with this map. In the left-hand side corner at the bottom, we see a scale used to determine the distance of any two points. Can you see that, Mr. Janc?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Based on that, can you tell us what was the width and length of the Srebrenica enclave if we were to use this particular scale because a red line -- sorry, please go ahead. A red line on the scale is the size of 1 kilometre, you can see what the ratio is. Since you are an expert in maps, can you tell us approximately what was the length and width of the zone?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Objection. That is readily evident by the map itself. I don't understand the utility of such a question. It's right there in front of us. It's no test of credibility or anything else.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If you want to have a comment on the map, then you should put a question to that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Since Mr. McCloskey said that it was evident, could we just have the witness tell us the evident part, what he can see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we all can see the map, the lines on the map, the dots, and the scale on the left-hand bottom corner. I think this is really sufficient for your purposes. And now in connection to that, put your question, please. The witness is not here for counting.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, can you tell us, as an OTP investigator, whether you know that the Srebrenica enclave, as of May 1993 up until June 1995, was enlarged by some 150 square kilometres? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I cannot comment on that. I'm not aware of the exact enlargement. There might be some but I'm not sure about it, so I would rather not comment on that. But I think the witnesses will come to explain this in detail in this case because they were studying this issue also.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Janc.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown map number 11 from the map book that was proposed for admittance by the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It might be in e-court, page number 13.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This is a map that the witness said was a map of the western Balkans. Maybe that can be of assistance, thank you. So map number 1 from the map book. Thank you. This is for the transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We have one map on the screen before us. Is that what you are asking for? No, it is not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think he is looking for e-court number 3.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. McCloskey. Thank you, that is the map that we have before us now in e-court.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like the witness to tell us why he used a New York Times map of the former Socialist Federal Republic of Yugoslavia? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think this map was obtained a long time ago by the Tribunal, and it was used for most of the cases so far, and as well as for this case. There is no particular reason why we have used this map, so it's just the matter that this one was available and we have used that one.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I can't read New York Times. It's written here "The Times" map of the western Balkans. "The Times". Just for clarification.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: The witness can, perhaps, clarify and tell us whether this is a map taken from the New York Times, or rather, I apologise, from "The Times," and here we have a smaller version of that map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, that one, as I understand it, this map was produced by "The Times," and then it was publicly available and someone bought it here from the Tribunal and rescan it and now it's used.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us for the transcript, please, what year this map was produced in? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I will try to find this information from the map itself, but there is no such information, so I am afraid I cannot produce this information, but, as I was told by the one who bought this map, it was bought in 1994, so it must be produced around that time or before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps I can be of assistance. You provided to my legal advisor a copy of a map which reads, "Zagreb 1993." So would you agree with me that this map was produced in Zagreb in 1993 and then republished in "The Times"? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's speculation, but I can agree if that's the same map and everything there is the same, it can be, indeed, the case that it was produced in 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you just tell us for the transcript whether in addition to the former republics, Yugoslav Republics, the map of the western Balkans also includes some other states? And if so, what are they? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's, I think, difficult to answer, which part of the western Balkan. So I don't know the exact country which are part of it, because I know even for my country, Slovenia, sometimes they say it is, sometimes they say it's not. So I cannot say anything about it. So, but I think most of the republics we can see on this map, they are part of it, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. We can see Slovenia here as well. Does Slovenia belong to this same region? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've just given the answer to that, that some people say yes, it is part of it, some people say it's not, so it's somewhere there, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So would this then be a political or geographic issue, because we are discussing geography here? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say, you know, the opinion in my country, so I think it more relates to what the people would rather see than what is indeed the case. So, but, yes, what we were -- what we have learned in our schools, it is part of the western Balkan.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Because when I went to school and learned, the Balkans is a mountain and that is how the Balkan peninsula actually got it's name. Now that same mountain is called the Stara Planina, the old mountain, and it is in Bulgaria, and it stretches all the way to the Black Sea. My question for you is: As an investigator for the OTP, did the indication of the countries of Eastern Europe, which are not members of the European Unions, and when you indicated those states that are members of the European Union, did you actually adapt this map to reflect that?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Did the European Union use those terms for non-European members, non-European Union members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I'm not aware of that, so, sorry, I cannot answer what these European Union used for their purposes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. But my question is: Did you, as an OTP investigator, refer to this area of the western Balkans as countries of the south-eastern Europe, those are that not members of the European Union, and is that a political rather than a geographic term to determine the geographic position of those countries? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's rather the geographical position, geographical term of these countries.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did Slovenia in the past belong to this geographic region of the Balkan states?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think the country was always there at the same place.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Very well. We will now move on to this small map in the lower left corner in order to see whether there are any other points that we differ or can agree on. The Prosecutor's choice to use this map as evidence in this case, we would like to try and use this map which shows the ethnic composition. And I'm referring to the small map. I do not expect you to give me specific answers, but just some general answers which I'm sure you will be able to provide as an OTP investigator. My first question is this: Could you please read for us from this map the ethnic groups that are listed on the left-hand side of the map, and if you can't see it clearly, perhaps we can zoom in on the smaller map. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, it's hard to see. I would rather see the zoom in, but I am afraid it would be the same. I can try.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Excuse me. As I mentioned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: -- this little corner of the map was never something that the Prosecution intended. If General Tolimir -- we can agree right now that this is not part of the evidence of the case and it can be disregarded, if that's what he would prefer. It was never meant to be part of the case. If he wants to use it as his part of the case, that's, of course, his prerogative, but I can agree with him that it's not part of the case, if he would like. It's really not readable in this context, and I'm sure we could come up with one that is readable, but it was never meant to be part of the Prosecution's case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We heard your position, Mr. McCloskey, already earlier, but on the other hand, you provided this map which was created by "The Times" to the Chamber and the parties, and if the -- Mr. Tolimir want to use it, I think, during cross-examination, he may put some questions to that to the witness. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. Could the witness please, Mr. Janc, answer the question, and if he cannot see clearly, my legal assistant has a blown up copy of that map from which he can read. Would you allow us to provide this to the witness so he can answer my question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Yes, please. But through the ...

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I have it here now, and I see it's the same. And I can read it from here. So from the left-hand side, I'll go from the top to the bottom. The nations and national minorities. First one, Croats, Macedonians, Montenegrins, Muslims, Serbs, Slovenes, Albanians, Bulgarians, Czechs, Hungarians, Italians, gypsies, Romanians, Ruthenians, Slovaks, Turks, Vlachs, Yugoslavs and regional affiliation.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. So you can read this, because at the time when this map was tendered it was said that it cannot even be read. But my next question to you is this: Mr. Janc, what is the difference between the ethnic aspect and the religious affiliation on the other hand, if you can answer that question, thank you; if not, thank you in any case.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would rather not because I'm not an expert in that field. So I would avoid these kind of questions. I mean answers.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us what the difference is between the groups under number 4 and 16? Under number 4 we have Muslims, and under 16 we have Turks.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So the same as before, so I would not rather answer this question because I'm, indeed, not expert in this field, especially not in other part in Slovenia, so I know there two minorities in Slovenia [indiscernible] Italian and Hungarian, and that's all I would -- can comment about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us, please, as an OTP investigator, where Muslims and how they happen to be in the Balkans? Where they came from. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a historical question, so and, again, I'm not an expert in that field in history, so I would rather avoid it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell us whether the Muslims in this area that we are talking about, and that is an issue here in this trial, as an ethnic group actually came into existence after the Turks came to the Balkans? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The same as before, I cannot comment on this because simply I'm not very well educated in this field.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you answer this question: Did the Islam faith, as shown on this map, come to this area with the Turks, and did they force the local population because they were the power, the -- they were the occupying power, did they force the local population to take on that new faith?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, I think this is far beyond what you can expect from this witness. Several times he explained he is not a historical expert, not a religious expert, not a expert on ethnological questions. You should really focus on his expertise and his evidence in chief. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President. I only asked about this exhibit which shows the ethnic composition, and I just asked this witness because this exhibit was actually tendered through this witness to try and answer this question. But I can move on to another question. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It is very important because we will see documents here where we will find indication printed or handwritten where the terms Muslims and Turks are used as synonymous, and it is very important for us to hear from this witness, because it is through this witness that this map is being tendered, to explain these terms. And if you feel there is no need for that, that's all right, but I'm just saying that there will be other documents where we will see these terms used, and I believe this witness can or should explain it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you going to put a question to the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness just draw on this map the areas where these ethnic groups shown under the legend, can he mark those ethnic groups on the map. Thank you. Can he show where they were actually deployed. And if that's a problem, could he just indicate where the Turks were, just this one ethnic group. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is no longer appropriate, Mr. Tolimir, because it is very clear that this witness didn't produce this map. It was received by the Prosecution from the magazine, "The Times", and it was not used in any way by the Prosecution in examination-in-chief. The witness could only do what everybody could do, and if you compare the legend and the colours, I don't do that, then you can draw your conclusion by yourself. The witness is not helpful in that way. Please carry on. Your question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The map that we have here, which was tendered as an exhibit, shows where these groups can be found, and that is why I'm putting these questions about this exhibit; and if you allow me, I feel that this is an issue that will be of interest and that is at issue in this trial. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please put a question to the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you explain for this Chamber what the term "Yugoslav" refers to. So we'll move on from the Turks and Muslims to Yugoslavs. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, the same as before, I'm not an expert in that field, so I would avoid that answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. That may be very relevant because they kept changing sides in the conflict, including in this war and this will be relevant when we discuss the groups in the course of this trial. Thank you. Now, just can you answer this: Did the data provided on this map, or actually, did you compare the data from this map to the data as provided by the 1991 census? Thank you. And this census was recognised by all the Yugoslav Republics.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: If you mean this ethnic composition map, no, I didn't do that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I did mean the ethnic composition. I would also like to ask you whether the facts, as shown here about the ethnic groups, were compared to the censuses that were conducted in the republics after 1995 after the war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness now please be shown map number 9 entitled, "Deployment of Hours, Enemy as well as UNPROFOR Forces." Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is this a military map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, this is a military map. VRS military map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do commanders use military maps to provide reliable information on the situation in the territory shown on that map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, we are again coming to the expertise. I'm not an expert on, so I would rather avoid this question, and that you ask some military expert about it because I'm more investigative expert than a military expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you then, at least, tell us how you got this map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map was seised or obtained together with VRS Drina Corps collection in 2004. And the original is on my left-hand side.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we next see map number 10, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Should be e-court page number 12.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we please enlarge the map so as to be able to see what is written on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, have you ever seen the coat of arms of Republika Srpska or the FRY or any state populated by Serbs, for that matter?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said here that we see the four Ss on that map, you stated that for the record; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. That's what we can see on this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. What do you base your conclusion on because there are no four Ss here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is a cross and inside the cross there are four Ss, these are Cyrillic letters. I am aware of that fact that this is written in Cyrillic.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can one write the letter S the other way around, as is the case with the two left-hand side semicircles on this cross?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, you are right. I think I'm not. Only what is on the right-hand side. This is S or Latin C, that is Cyrillic S; so on the left-hand side, we have, you know, other way around, so again I would not rather go into discussion about the Cyrillic language and script because definitely I'm not an expert in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. I'd rather not have gone into this topic had you not mentioned it, and I believe it is necessary to explain the four letters that we can see here. As you have identified already, there are no four Ss here, as a matter of fact there are only two; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, if you say so, that's your script, so I can agree with you, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you tell me this: Did you know that as of 1402, each and every Serbian state in its coat of arms contained a similar sign, a similar symbol, the symbol of the cross with the four "ocilos"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: O-c-i-l-o-s.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of that.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness please be shown 1D80. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you see the cross and four "ocilos" in front of you on the screen?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the cross and some letters in it, so which looks like "E" to me, so.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that this was the coat of arm of the new Byzantine empire as it appeared on their flag in the 14th century?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This was the flag of the Byzantine empire. It meant, [B/C/S spoken] meaning, translated, the emperor of emperors governs the empires. Hence, it has nothing to do with the letter S or Serbs, it was simply copied from the Byzantine flag dating back to the 14th century.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I would request the ability to cross-examine Mr. Tolimir. If he is going to continue to testify, I should have the right to cross-examine him or he should indicate that he is providing statements pursuant to the Rule that allows him to do so; but not in this manner, it's not relevant the way he is doing it now. If he is continuing, I would like to cross-examine him on this issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please put questions to this witness.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I asked him whether he knew that this was the new coat of arms of the Byzantine empire in the 14th century.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And he answered this question. He didn't know. Please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Do you know what, in Byzantine, it means [B/C/S spoken]?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not at all.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you know that these Byzantine words had nothing to do with the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: He answered already that he didn't know. You should leave this topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will move on to another topic, but I merely wanted to point out that these words and these signs speak for themselves, so as not to be misled about the symbol itself. This is the sign of a cross --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it's not necessary to explain anything further. Just put questions to this witness which are relevant for this witness and for you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Witness, the marking on the map as it is, the sign of the cross and the four "ocilos," could we deem it to be a symbol of the Serbs or Serbhood?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In military practice, is it customary to use simplified symbols such as flags and coats of arms to mark territories which a certain armed force controls?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am afraid it's again a question for a military expert. I cannot comment on it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you comment this: Do you know or do you believe that in any territory liberated in the course of an armed conflict is marked by a symbol of the force taking control of that territory? If you know an answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not aware of any, so I cannot help you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. In Slovenia, after it's cessation from the SFRY, did it change its flag and coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember that was the case, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does any armed force have the right to mark its territory it had taken over?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, again, regarding the arms forces, I am not an expert on, so I cannot comment on this question again.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Perhaps this question will clarify it. Did General Krstic write anything on the map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on this one, yes, we can see his handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Precisely. He also wrote a date, the 27th of July, 1995. He signed it, stamped it with the stamp of the VRS. Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. The drawing Krstic made, is it a simplified Serbian coat of arms, indicating that on that day it became part of the territory of Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We first clarify, which map you are referring to in the moment, and could we have that on the screen again, please. Is it that map on the left side of the screen?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. The map is on the witness's left-hand side. He can see it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Are you referring to the map now on the screen? Have a look on the screen, please, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Yes, I am referring to the map on the screen. If we move slightly to the right --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I think what we are looking for is the electronic version of the map, not the map book reproduction. 933. Back to that one again.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. We still waiting for 933.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will appear on the screen. Judge Nyambe has a question to that. Perhaps we can --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, that is the map.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Remove the flag on the right-hand side so that we have more -- yes, thank you. Now a question by Judge Nyambe.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Actually my question has been answered by the enlargement of the map because I was looking for the signature made by the General on the map. But, maybe, just for the avoidance of doubt, if you can indicate on the map where you say the General signed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I can make a circle around it. Just a second. Okay. There are two signatures. The first one is up here and the stamp underneath. And the second one is here. So these are his signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NYAMBE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, for clarification should we receive that as an exhibit? You are not tendering it?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have no objection to having this admitted. I merely wanted to state -- well, I see Mr. McCloskey is on his feet, and I will then state my argument.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: We agree with the General that this should be admitted. I would also ask the General if he is agreeing that this is an authentic VRS map signed, in fact, by General Krstic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. McCloskey, the accused is not a witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
