utterances.text: As a representative of himself, I'm asking for a stipulation on a matter of evidence. Since he is offering it into evidence, it's incumbent upon him to prove its authenticity. And I think it's something we agree on, that is all I'm asking. He seems to be implying that in his questions, so I'm taking this opportunity, because I don't see him otherwise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would you like to comment on that, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly. I only wanted to ask the witness about something that found its way into the transcript. I wanted to ask those two questions, by your leave, which have to do with this part of the map, in view of Judge Nyambe's question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, I believe it's incumbent upon Mr. Tolimir, representing himself, to tell the Court, as he is offering this into evidence, whether he believes it's authentic or not. That's just a foundational issue. He should be able to tell you whether he believes this to be authentic. If he thinks it's a falsehood or some creation of the Prosecution, we should know that as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The Chamber states that no party tendered the marking on the map as an exhibit, but we have the explanation of everybody on the record, and I think, Mr. McCloskey, it is not appropriate to ask questions to the accused about his opinion if he can state something. Earlier today, you, yourself, indicated that the accused is not a witness, he is not in the position to give a statement; therefore, it's not appropriate to put this request to him by you. That's the position of this Chamber, and I think we should carry on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. Then I must change my position and object to his offering this into evidence, giving no foundation whatsoever for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It's also the position of the Chamber, the map with the markings will not be received as an exhibit. Mr. Tolimir, please carry on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I have stated already that I put these questions because of the transcript, not because of the map itself. When the witness was questioned by the OTP, the transcript reflected that he had stated that these were the four Ss; but if you ask any Serb, he or she would never say that these were four Ss but only two, on the left-hand side, there are two letters which are not part of our alphabet --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: We are not interested in any discussion about what happened in the court. I think we are running out of time. We must have our second break now. And, please, then prepare further cross-examination and put questions to this witness. We should have a certain progress. Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: [Overlapping speakers] ...

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I conclude this topic with two brief questions which could be answered with a yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, we resume now and resume at ten minutes past 6.00, and then you can put the relevant questions to the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, please carry on with your questions for the witness, but bear in mind, in fact you have 30 minutes left. You indicated two hours and --

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: I would like to ask the witness, as I see and look at this map and everything that is written on it, whether after everything that has been said here, this still resembles the four Ss or, in fact, some other symbol or mark?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may also be some other mark because I'm not an expert in these marks so it can be.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, the marking from topography where crosses are used as well, actually, would it be of any assistance if you read what is written to the right of this mark?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't read it from here, so I would rather get the translation, so I cannot read the Cyrillic not very well, so I cannot read what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Have you prepared the translation of these maps for the Trial Chamber, the English translation? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think there it is one. It was on the screen before, so there should be one, the translation of this map.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If the Trial Chamber needs it, can we have this translation, although we've seen it before. If not, I can read what is written there. It says, and there is a signature and stamp by General-Major Krstic, "Srebrenica was Serbian and is Serbian now. The 12th of July, 1995." And at the bottom it says, "Zepa too is Serbian, 27th of July, 1995." Major-General Radislav Krstic, who also affixed a stamp there. And we see on the stamp, we also see the symbol that is now shown in its graphic form on the map. Is it correct that what I've read out is what is actually written here on the map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I agree with you, it's correct.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown 1D, pages 82 and 83. And 4, 84.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Here we see the fourth page. Can you see the cross on this coat of arms?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is this the coat of arms of the Republika Srpska? Is this the official coat of arms and have you seen it before?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've seen it before, and I think it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Does this symbol on the map on the left-hand side coincide, is it similar to the symbol that we see here on this coat arms?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, part of it. It's similar. It's a cross and these four letters there. That's similar, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see number 3 from document 1D80. And number 2.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: What can we see here, what can you tell us?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we please see the image that we just saw before this one. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Now, what can you see here?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Actually, it should be a symbol from, I don't know, it's my pure speculation now, but from the area of former Yugoslavia somewhere. I don't know from. It's written there from 1804 up to 1941, so, I haven't seen this symbol before.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. This symbol actually represents the coat of arms of the Socialist Republic of Serbia from 1963 when Serbia was part of the same country that Slovenia was part of. We can see it in English as well. Thank you. Now, can we see on this coat of arms a similar symbol as the one that we see on the map?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, the letters are similar. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we now please see page 2 of this document. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us what we see before us now?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's written down underneath, so it's coat of arms of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Is that the official coat of arms of the Republic of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Again, I'm not an expert in that, but I think it is, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Do we see on it the same symbol as we see on the map? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this document, 1D80 into evidence. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D22, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could the witness now please be shown map number 11. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: E-court it should be page number 13 [Realtime transcript read in error "30"].

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you show or indicate here where the hill, the highest elevation point above Zepa is?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused please repeat the name of the elevation.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you now please mark it because we'll need this for the witnesses that are yet to come. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can you repeat which hill, the name of the hill?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Zlovrh. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can. I'll mark it.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. You said here --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, it's still not marked yet.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Marks]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: I'd just like to make a correction at line 16, page 60, it's recorded page number 30, but it's page number 13. Just for clarification. Please carry on, Mr. Tolimir.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, please tell us why did you measure the distance driving a vehicle between places, and did this reflect the actual situation as it was at the time of the conflicts in terms of the road conditions? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yeah, we measured these distances just to get a sense of it how far these places are from each other; and, of course, we took into considerations that the conditions are most probably not the same as they were in 1995, so that's why I emphasised last time that these are rough estimates.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you measure the distance between Borik, Kravica and Pilica? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that distance was not measured. But I think that we provide -- I'm not sure with this map, but I know we have distances between these places which can be provided.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please be shown map number 9. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Tolimir, do you tender this map marked by the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: It will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D23, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Could we now please see map number 9. Enlarged.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Please mark on this map, if you can, Borik, Potocari, Kravica, and Branjevo. Can you mark it in green ink, thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can, but I think -- just a second. I will start with Borik.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Borik, that's in the Zepa area.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, can we scroll down a little bit. Yes. I circled here, it's a little bit more left, just a few centimetres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Would you now, please, in the Srebrenica area mark Kravica, Borik, Pilica, and Potocari. Kravica, Pilica, Potocari and Branjevo. Not Borik, sorry. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Just a second, I'll put Borik as B here, so that's Borik area. And for the Srebrenica part, we would need to scroll up.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: The problem, if you do that, you will lose the markings. Mr. Tolimir, it would be helpful if we could receive this marking as a separate exhibit and then carry on with the other markings you wish to get.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. For us it would be useful to have all these markings on one and the same map for the witnesses that are yet to come, so if possible, could he please mark the areas in Srebrenica and then we can deal with Borik later on more easily. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If we want to have everything on the same map, we should start again from the beginning, scroll down a little bit and the witness is asked to mark the location again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Mr. President, all these locations are not on this map. There is one map in the book where all of the locations are already listed, that may be more helpful. But it's clear no matter where you scroll this map, you are not going to see some of these locations on it. So perhaps if we -- if he looks at e-court map number 10, which is page 8, all those locations he is interested are clearly there on that map and a legend that shows how far they are.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Would that be helpful for you, Mr. Tolimir? Perhaps easier. Could we have that map on the screen.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I agree. So let the witness be shown map number 10. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Page number 12 of this exhibit.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: It's actually page 8 of the exhibit, e-court number 10. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Now it's clear.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: You had the green one, it's the light green one. E-court number 10, you had it for awhile and you need to make it a little bit smaller, a little bit smaller than that and you'll see the whole region, Rogatica to Bijeljina and beyond.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But not all the locations Mr. Tolimir has indicated.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: I'm sure Mr. Janc can help Mr. Tolimir with anything that is not listed on the map. You got the major locations, but Mr. Janc will, I'm sure, be able to help.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: If that could be zoomed in a little bit and the relevant area. Yes. Perhaps now the witness can mark the locations of the different villages.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can mark almost all of them on this picture, but Branjevo. I can see it's further north, but I can do for the others, if that helps.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you, that will be helpful for our upcoming witnesses. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'll start with Borik. Down on the south.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: You should put a number 1.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. Number 1 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This is Borik.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: -- is for Borik. Then next one I requested was, I think, Kravica. We can see Kravica here, it's written.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Just encircle it, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: And this is number 2. Then we have Potocari, I think it was also the place. Potocari, number 3. And which else was requested?

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Branjevo.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, Branjevo is -- I cannot see it on this map, it's further north, north of Zvornik, so we have to save this first and then try with another one.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the witness kindly lean back because there's a feedback effect. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Indicate with an arrow the direction where it is. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Please put the name of Branjevo somewhere on the top of the map. Put a number 4 to that and perhaps an arrow in which direction it should be. Is that sufficient, Mr. Tolimir?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, that is sufficient.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: And I would just ask the witness to also indicate the axis of movement from Srebrenica towards Tuzla which the BH Army column actually travelled along. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So it's this direction to the north. It's number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you please write in your own handwriting "Tuzla" on the very outer rim of the map up there. Above Zvornik, if you can write Tuzla so we just know that that is the general direction, that this is in the direction of Tuzla. Thank you. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to tender this into evidence for use with future witnesses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This marked map will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D25, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Can you tell us how many people worked on preparing this collection of maps?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say four or five, something like that. But some of them were created already before, so at least five.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Tell us, please, why is it that you did not produce a map showing the BH Army column as an actual force that was on the ground at the time?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But there is a map with arrows showing the BH Army column and which is going from Srebrenica up to the north. There is a map number 5 and 6, I would say.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we then pull up that map, please, where we can see the arrows indicating the movement of the column. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Map 5 is e-court 7.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yeah, I think the best map is number 5. And we can see here red arrows, so that is the movement of the column.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. If you can, could you please produce another map where you would show the movement of the column, a geographic map, or if not, could you please just indicate on this map column of the BH Army so that we know what these red arrows actually stand for.

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can write if you want, but the other map is this map, Krivaja 1995 map. So where you have the blue arrows going down from Srebrenica up to Baljkovica, so the other reference would be that map.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: That's 65 ter 907.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Could you please mark on this map these arrows that represent the column. Can you write on the right-hand side the column, and then above that where the red arrows are, just can you write "BH Army," or "ABiH."

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: The legend of the map says direction of Muslim column with a red arrow. So I don't think that's necessary.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: But, Mr. McCloskey, it was asked for an indication of the movement of the BiH army. That might be a different wording, but why shouldn't the witness not mark it as requested by the accused.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can mark it, but it's Muslim column. It's for both BH Army and the civilians, but I can do additional marking here saying that's column. And what is -- something else was requested to be put, let me check --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Well, actually what I would like you to write is ABiH column, but as you want to also add civilians, you can write the column ABiH, but I don't know whether these were civilians or conscripts because all conscripts, able-bodied men were called up to join that column and we've heard witnesses testify about that. And this is really to assist future witnesses because they can't really read maps very well. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: This witness can only mark according to his evidence. Mr. Janc, do you mean by column also the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, indeed both. BiH army and these civilians, so that refers to both of them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: And then we have it on the record, and I think that is sufficient. Do you tender this map with the marking column?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, yes, Mr. President. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you, it will be received.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As Exhibit D24, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the accused kindly lean back. He is creating a feedback because he is too close to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm having feedback whenever I turn the mike on. Somebody has their microphone on?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: There was some confusion about the number, but Mr. Tolimir, when you speak, please not too near to the microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, it seems to be fine now. Somebody's microphone was on. By your leave, I have two more questions of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Were you in the area of Zepa, Witness?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, indeed, several times.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Did you travel from the area of Zepa towards Srebrenica?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but only, I took one direction through Rogatica.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Did you indicate that distance where you indicated the others?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, that distance is not indicated here in our -- in our chart, but I measured that distance, and I think it's -- if you go over Rogatica, I can tell you it's around 160 kilometres, something like that. If you go different route up to the north towards Han Pijesak, not around Rogatica, it's closer, around 130 kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Thank you. Can the shorter route of 130 kilometres be used?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it can be used for sure. I was travelling down from --

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Is it a forest-path or a regular road that can be used for travel?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's an asphalt road now through forest and you can travel easily. I was doing it even in winter conditions, so it's quite a decent road now.

utterances.speaker: MR. TOLIMIR
utterances.text: Was there any asphalt there during the war?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: That I don't know, but I assume not because now the road is -- it looks very, very, fresh, it looks a new one, so it might be a renovated one, or, you know, the asphalt might be just new. I cannot -- I don't know what was there during the war. I don't have this information.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, since I've exhausted the time allocated to me, I'd like to thank the witness for the production of these maps and the assistance he provided and will be providing during the proceedings. I would also like to thank the Chamber for their understanding and patience. This closes my cross-examination. I would also like to thank all those who assisted me in doing so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. McCloskey, do you have re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Just very, very, briefly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Witness, have you heard of the Serbian phrase "Samo Sloga Srbina Spasava"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: And perhaps translations can help me and just translate this "Samo Sloga Srbina Spasava"?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Only concord saves the Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: What does that term mean to you in English? Just the meaning. I'm not trying to get into the history or anything deeper, just what the words translates to in English?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know it refers to that symbol we have been talking about, so I know that everybody refers to it as a phrase for the symbol; so, no, I cannot explain the meaning of it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Have you heard "only unity can save the Serbs"?

utterances.speaker: DUSAN JANC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's also sometimes referred as for this symbol.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Nothing further, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. Janc, thank you very much. This concludes your examination. The Chamber thanks you for your attendance two times to the court and you are free now to return to your normal work with the OTP. Thank you very much again.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: Mr. McCloskey, I think it's ten minutes before 7.00, only ten minutes left.

utterances.speaker: MR. MCCLOSKEY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. President, we had a 15 minute video so we don't have enough time, it's a 20 minute video, so we would suggest that we be done.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
utterances.text: In that case, we have to adjourn for today and resume on Monday at 9.00. We have no hearing tomorrow. We explained that earlier. Thank you very much. We adjourn.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE FLUEGGE
